## session: codex adapter v2 (hooks, skills, gcc outbox) [codex-gcc-7a] 2026-09-10

**Purpose:** wire the gcc into Codex CLI 0.153.4: symlinked skills, hooks and rules, wrapped guards, claude-ipc identity, ledger writes through an outbox.

**Insights:**

1. The Aug-14 "codex hooks never fire" verdict was two things at once: a snake_case hooks file that parsed but matched nothing, and the per-hash hook trust gate that skips untrusted hooks with no warning under `exec`. A canary hook that denies a unique string, run through `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`, settles it in one run. `-c bypass_hook_trust=true` does not work.
2. Codex's hook stdin payload matches Claude Code's (session_id, cwd, tool_name Bash, tool_input.command) and it accepts the old `{"decision":"block"}` shape, so gcc guard scripts run unchanged behind a shim that only re-keys the environment.
3. Codex inherits the launching Claude session's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; the seat's own id is `CODEX_THREAD_ID` (the same value as the hook session_id). Any gcc tool keyed on the env var must be re-keyed or it acts as the parent. A direct `claude-ipc register` would rebind the parent's mailbox.
4. The sandbox blocks writes outside the workspace and /tmp and blocks the ipc socket, but hooks run outside the sandbox. An outbox in /tmp drained by an async PostToolUse hook lands a queued write within seconds and can inject the receipt mid-turn. No network grant needed.
5. `codex debug prompt-input` looked like an offline way to verify the skills list but takes no `-C`. Skill discovery was verified by asking the model to list its skills instead.
6. Two hook layers holding the same file (user layer plus a trusted project layer) fire each hook twice. Keep hooks at one layer.

## session: finish the queue, then core-dump with next-session scope [guard-bad-e3], 2026-09-09

Purpose: under the owner's armed goal, close every agent-reachable row with a tested mechanism, then dump with the owner's three next-session items named.

Insights:
- The caveat differ matches on 60% word overlap with one middle-dot-separated chunk, not verbatim, but a retirement chain from a prior dump is one huge chunk, so accounting for it needs its words present. Quote a retired blob whole; a paraphrase never clears it.
- An honest fix to a seven-day windowed check is a companion window, not a moved verdict: keep the red, append the since-fix number. It showed the close verb took (135/136) and the goal-proposal gate has not (2/23, because a running session loads settings once at start).
- A store sidecar must not end in .json: pathlib globs dotfiles where the shell and glob.glob do not, so .goals.json rendered as a task row.
- The owner will paste an approval line four times in a session without complaint; the typed-line push channel is the surface he actually uses, and it never halts the turn.
- The Stop hook kept blocking on "Finish all" while the reachable work was done; the honest close is that the remainder is owner-gated (the push), time-gated (09-15), or the owner's own next-session scope, not more agent work to invent.

## session: finish the agent-ready queue and check it against the behavioural goal [guard-bad-e3], 2026-09-08

Purpose: resume push-guard-7c's checkpoint, close every agent-ready row in store cd22422c with a tested mechanism, then say where the behavioural goal still has gaps.

Insights:
- pathlib's `*.json` glob matches dotfiles; the shell's and glob.glob's do not. A store sidecar named `.goals.json` was read as a task row on the first render. The sidecar is `.goals` and the loader skips dotfiles.
- A checkpoint's "suite N/0" is true of the tree it was measured on. goal-box.test.sh had two cases red at HEAD when the footer gained its "today" line; the count in the checkpoint was stale by one commit.
- The done-row ball (✅) at the row position is not enough to call a line a row: the new `✅ when:` line matched case 18's empty-box detector and hid a real V1 defect in a mutant. Detectors should require ball, twin and id.
- The renderer's fixed-point reservation absorbs a small under-pricing by refusing the box on the next pass, so an unpriced-box mutant's symptom is an empty box, never a height overrun. Detect the defect, not the height.
- A Stop hook's block output may be pretty-printed (`jq -n`) or compact (`jq -cn`); a test pattern that assumes one shape reads a working block as a miss.
- The wake fence for the lanes is skill text only: forge-console's transcript holds 76 wake prompts and zero copies of the fence sentence. Armed crons carry the old text until they re-arm.
